last_material_result: Final mutation #3 tested a late-night taxi split/fallback wedge: venue + destination direction + party size + Seoul late-night taxi surcharge + last usable transit hub => compare full taxi versus transit-to-last-hub plus split taxi. KILL. The underlying late-night fare calculation is already commoditized by multiple consumer taxi calculators, while making the proposed answer genuinely useful requires route-specific distance/time to candidate hubs and live or frequently maintained last-train feasibility. Without routing data the result collapses into a generic taxi-fare calculator; with routing/transit data it violates the bounded-maintenance advantage of this incubation lane. This is the third materially different concert-return wedge to fail after event-specific safe-leave cutoff and door-to-door same-day-return feasibility. The consumer pain is real, but the acquisition/data-maintenance whitespace is insufficient, so the entire concert-return cluster is closed rather than forced into BUILD.
economics: KRW0 spent. Generic taxi-fare calculators already cover Seoul fare and late-night surcharge calculations, compressing differentiation and SEO upside. A defensible transit-hub fallback calculator would add route/schedule maintenance disproportionate to the likely KRW10k-50k/month micro-asset contribution target. Expected contribution-adjusted EV is therefore below fresh discovery.
next_checkpoint: Next run return to fresh Lane A genetic discovery. Rotate away from concert/event-return transport and prefer a local/everyday consumer utility with public/free data, a concrete recurring decision, bounded maintenance and clearer distribution whitespace.
recommendation: KILL the Seoul Venue Encore Cutoff / concert-return pain cluster after three distinct wedges failed. Start fresh discovery next run; do not revisit this cluster absent materially new capability or distribution evidence.
